analysis:
Step 1 – Degree: strong (Industrial Engineering). Python/pandas: strong (forecasting project on 2 years × 12 stores). SQL: weak — only 'SQL (basic)' in skills, no usage. BI tool: weak — Power BI listed, dashboard project lacks tool and detail. Excel: medium — weekly stock reports, pivot tables. Communication: medium — presented to an operations manager. English: strong (IELTS 6.5).
Step 2 – Depth: the forecasting project is the best evidence but ends with 'better than the old method' — no metric, no model type. Internship bullets are duties, not results.
Step 3 – Seniority: well matched for a junior role; supply-chain internship and certificate are a plus.
Step 4 – Credible junior with real retail-like data experience; SQL is the main gap for a role built around a PostgreSQL warehouse.
verdict: Credible junior candidate with relevant forecasting experience, but SQL — a daily tool in this role — is not demonstrated.

strengths.point: Hands-on analysis of realistic retail data, directly relevant to our clients.
strengths.evidence: Used Python (pandas) to analyse 2 years of daily sales data from 12 stores.

strengths.point: Experience presenting results to a business stakeholder.
strengths.evidence: Presented results to the company's operations manager.

strengths.point: Inventory reporting experience matches our recurring sales and inventory reports.
strengths.evidence: Responsible for preparing weekly stock reports in Excel.

issues.problem: The role writes SQL against a PostgreSQL warehouse every day, but the CV gives no example of SQL use.
issues.fix: If any project or course used SQL, describe it in a bullet (tables, joins, what question it answered). If not, a small public project (e.g. SQL analysis of an open retail dataset on GitHub) would close this gap.

issues.evidence: Built a forecasting model that was better than the old method.
issues.problem: I cannot judge the depth of the forecasting work: which model, which metric, how much better?
issues.fix: Name the method you used and the metric you measured, e.g. 'Built a [model type] model that reduced forecast error (MAPE) from [X%] to [Y%]' — fill in only true values.

issues.evidence: Made a dashboard about Istanbul traffic data.
issues.problem: A dashboard project is relevant, but there is no tool, data source, audience or insight, so it does not prove BI skills.
issues.fix: Add the tool, data source and one insight it revealed, in one or two bullets — only what you actually did.

issues.evidence: Helped the team with data entry and cleaning of supplier data.
issues.problem: Data cleaning is a core part of this job, but 'helped with' hides your own contribution.
issues.fix: Describe what you cleaned and how (Excel functions, rules, number of records), using only facts you can explain in an interview.
